x: A couple of miles into the National Junior Cross Country Championships at Parliament Hill and Belgrave's Kaessa Tadesse leads Coventry Godiva's Stefan White (186), the eventual winner , Blackheath's Tim Dickinson (behind), who ended up 4th, and 'Southern' winner Spencer Barden (242) of GEC Avionics, 3rd.

But this was not the only talking point among the bystanders: a new Belgravian, Junior World Half-marathon Champion Kaessa Tadesse, an Ethiopian now settling in the UK, was making his Belgrave debut, and the field contained four ladies out to settle a few scores with male colleagues.

Gary Staines took another step up the ladder to peak fitness by sneaking under 30 minutes for 3rd place but had to sprint to make sure he was first Belgravian home, Kaessa Tadesse crossing the line just an eyelash behind.
The previous day Kaessa Tadesse, soon to join Belgrave, won the IAAF Junior Half Marathon Championship in the very impressive time of 64.51.

The dozen Belgravians involved in the Club Championship race for the "Blackstaffe" Shield took their places at the start line among many other runners taking part in the inter-club match to be held in conjunction but there was only ever going to be one winner of both events - Kaessa Tadesse.

Marcello, having had a miserable start to the afternoon after being held up in the traffic and failing to get Kaessa Tadesse to the start line in time for the Junior event was seen walking disconsolately away from the course while Marco also came out, visibly in pain with his back trouble having flared up again.
In the 8k race won in 23:28 by another Kenyan "find" Simon Chemnoyo, Kaessa Tadesse finished 44th in 25:12 and Marcello Bizio, representing Italy finished 93rd, 27:14.
However, although Gary comfortably won the race, and Kaessa Tadesse finding the conditions much more to his liking came second, it was really a matter of too little, too late.

Progression continued with John Gladwin, again only half fit, on the next short stage, and handing on to Kaessa Tadesse who had the difficult task of setting out just behind a bunch containing Andy Bristow and Dominic Bannister, the Southern champion.

Kaessa Tadesse was the pick of the rest of our long stage runners, benefiting from Steve's misfortune to become our fastest over the 5m 706y stretch with 26:06, and Johnny G took yet another step along the road to fitness by running a 14:50 effort that makes an appearance over 800m in our team for B…
